item.title: 🔴 NGINX2Root (CVE-2026-123007): Frequently asked questions about five critical NGINX vulnerabilities
item.description:
Why this matters: Remote-code-execution risk — assess exposure and patch or mitigate quickly.

Frequently asked questions about five critical NGINX remote code execution vulnerabilities and five additional flaws fixed in F5’s November 18 out-of-band release.

Key takeaways

  1. NGINX2Root is associated with five critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in NGINX, and a separate, unpatched Linux kernel local privilege escalation (LPE) flaw that can be chained with the NGINX bugs to gain root.
  2. CVE-2026-123007 is the most urgent of the five. It is an unauthenticated RCE flaw in NGINX’s HTTP/2 implementation and requires only HTTP/2 over TLS to be enabled. A PoC is publicly available on GitHub.
  3. F5’s November 18 release fixed the five NGINX2Root vulnerabilities and five additional NGINX flaws.

Background

Tenable’s Research Special Operations (RSO) team has compiled this blog to answer Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) regarding NGINX2Root, a set of five critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in NGINX, and five additional NGINX flaws that F5 fixed in an out-of-band security release on November 18, 2026.

item.title: 🟠 Oracle November 2026 Critical Security Patch Update Addresses 640 CVEs (CVE-2026-114938)
item.description:
Why this matters: Supply-chain risk — review third-party access and affected vendor dependencies.

Oracle addresses 640 CVEs in its November 2026 Critical Security Patch Update with 655 patches, including 62 critical updates.

Key Takeaways

  1. The November 2026 Critical Security Patch Update (CSPU) contains fixes for 640 unique CVEs in 655 security updates
  2. 62 issues (9.5% of all patches) were assigned a critical severity rating
  3. Oracle Hyperion received the highest number of patches at 267, accounting for 40.8% of all patches

Background

On November 17, Oracle released its Critical Security Patch Update (CSPU) for November 2026. Beginning in May 2026, Oracle introduced CSPUs as a monthly release cycle that sits between the larger quarterly Critical Patch Updates (CPUs), addressing a focused set of high-severity issues on a faster cadence. This CSPU contains fixes for 640 unique CVEs in 655 security updates across 21 Oracle product families. Out of the 655 security updates published, 9.5% of patches were assigned a critical severity. Medium severity patches accounted for the bulk of security patches at 41.8%, followed by high severity patches at 38%.

item.title: 🔴 Who Has Access to Claude? Bring AI Identity and Access Context Into Surface Command
item.description:
Why this matters: Potential data exposure — review monitoring and incident-response readiness.

Approving an AI service is only the starting point. As employees adopt Claude and their responsibilities change, security teams need to know who has access, which users hold administrative privileges, and whether those roles and group memberships still reflect the work they do.

IBM’s 2025 Cost of a Data Breach Report found that, among studied organizations reporting an AI-related breach, 97% lacked proper AI access controls. The finding highlights a broader challenge: AI adoption needs security practices that extend beyond the initial approval, supported by information teams can use to review access with administrators and service owners.

Rapid7 Surface Command now integrates with Claude’s Compliance API, bringing supported organization, user, role, group, and settings information into the same platform teams use to understand other assets and identities. The integration helps security teams make enterprise Clau…
